newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg expects low double-digit EPS rise in '97.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg expects low double-digit EPS rise in '97.

text.p: Kellogg Co said Friday it expects low double-digit percentage increase in earnings for 1997, following a disappointing 1996.
Kellogg spokesman Richard Lovell confirmed the projection, which had been reported earlier today by analysts.
According to First Call, the mean analyst earnings estimate for 1996 is $3.07 a share, down from $3.48 in 1995. The mean for 1997 is $3.48, matching the 1995 level.
Lovell also confirmed analysts' comments that Kellogg expects lower first quarter earnings compared with the $0.99 it earned in the 1996 period.
Previously, Kellogg had said 1996 first quarter earnings presented a challenge for 1997's opening quarter.
In the analyst meeting, Kellogg Chairman Arnold Langbo pledged that Kellogg will take the steps needed to regain market share, Lovell said.
But, as reported earlier, Langbo did not tell analysts what specific steps Kellogg would take.

"He (Langbo) indicated that we remain committed to our long-term strategy of lower cereal prices and reducing inefficient price promotion spending, introducing strong new products and cutting costs," Lovell said. "That's the long-term way to go."
Meanwhile, in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing Kellogg said it will eliminate about 600 additional employee positions by the end of 1997.
Lovell said most of the positions being eliminated are in international operations.
Kellogg has said it will cut about 2,000 positions by the end of 1996 as part of previously announced efforts to streamline operations.

As a result of those actions, Kellogg said it plans to take about $170 million in pretax charges in 1996, about $60.4 million of which have been taken thus far. The remaining charges are expected to be taken in the fourth quarter, Lovell said.
Kellogg took about $348 million in pretax charges in 1995 for the streamlining.
